summary.text: 家 is written with 宀 above 豕. The roof element fits the idea of a dwelling; the lower element has competing explanations—as a pig contributing to the scene or as a sound element related to 豭. Early uses for dwelling and household institutions are reported; today the character commonly means house, home, or family.

formation.text: The construction is disputed. One traditional analysis treats 宀 as the dwelling element and the lower form as an abbreviated 豭 used for sound. Other analyses read the lower form as a pig beneath a roof, or propose a pig enclosure as the original meaning. The latter proposal is not established, and the earliest role of the lower form remains uncertain.

components.text: 宀 is the roof or dwelling element in accounts of 家. It appears as a full component; no separate earlier form is proposed.

The lower component is written 豕. The traditional analysis treats it as an abbreviated 豭 used for sound; other accounts see a pig contributing to the scene. The proposed earlier sign 𢑓 and its alleged change into 豕 remain unverified.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin readings of 豭 and 家 match, as do their Middle Chinese and Old Chinese forms in the cited reconstruction system. This supports sound compatibility if 豭 is the relevant component, but does not establish the lower sign's earliest identity or provide a reading for proposed sign 𢑓.

sound.text: If 豭 is the relevant component, the cited reconstruction gives it the same Middle Chinese and Old Chinese forms as 家; their modern Mandarin readings also match. This supports compatibility, but does not assign a reading to visible 豕.
sound.system: Modern Mandarin; Middle Chinese and Old Chinese, Baxter–Sagart 2014

history.text: The traditional written analysis is 宀 with abbreviated 豭 as the sound element; the regular-script form writes 豕 below 宀. This records the traditional analysis and familiar written form, not proof of the earliest construction.
A claim that oracle-bone 𢑓 was the original lower sign and changed into 豕 through graphic corruption has not been verified from primary paleographic evidence.

uncertainties.text: The earliest identity and role of the lower element are unsettled. Some analyses connect it with 豭 as a sound element; others see a pig contributing to a meaningful scene and propose a pig enclosure as the origin. That proposed origin is not established.
Matching readings and reconstructions for 豭 and 家 do not prove that the earliest lower sign was named 豭. No independent ancient pronunciation for a proposed depicted animal or sign is established.

senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze uses are reported; sequence unresolved
senses.text: Reported uses include ancestral temple and family, royal house or court, and households counted as 家. Their order and relationships are not established.
家 commonly means house or home, and also family. How these current meanings connect to each reported early institutional use is not established.

developments.text: Dwelling and household or institutional uses are both reported early, but their sequence and any development from one to the other are not established.
Modern house, home, and family meanings are established, but the chronology and transitions linking them to early reported uses remain unclear.

limitations.text: The reported early uses do not provide a dated sequence of examined inscriptions. Individual examples and the chronology of meanings remain unresolved.

The pig-enclosure proposal connects a proposed early meaning to human dwelling; the traditional phonetic analysis instead explains the graph through sound. Neither account establishes a full chronology of the word's meanings.

components.text: 宀 contributes the roof or dwelling idea in the proposed construction.
